events.title: Tenochtitlan Falls to Spanish Forces
events.description: After a months-long siege, Spanish forces under Hernán Cortés and their indigenous allies took the Aztec capital of Tenochtitlan. The last Aztec ruler, Cuauhtémoc, was captured as he tried to flee across Lake Texcoco.
events.significance: The fall of the city ended the Aztec Empire and opened the way for three centuries of Spanish colonial rule in Mexico.

events.title: Victory at Blenheim
events.description: English and Imperial forces led by the Duke of Marlborough and Prince Eugene of Savoy defeated a Franco-Bavarian army near the Bavarian village of Blindheim, known in English as Blenheim.
events.significance: The victory broke the myth of French military invincibility. It also changed the course of the War of the Spanish Succession.

events.title: Alfred Hitchcock Is Born
events.description: Alfred Hitchcock was born in Leytonstone, on the outskirts of London. He became one of cinema's most celebrated directors.
events.significance: Hitchcock helped define the modern suspense thriller, and his visual style still influences filmmakers today.

events.title: Construction of the Berlin Wall Begins
events.description: In the early hours of the morning, East German troops began sealing off East Berlin from West Berlin. They began with barbed wire and soon replaced it with concrete.
events.significance: The Wall became the defining symbol of the Cold War's division of Europe. It stood until 1989.
